strengths: The paper addresses a relevant NLP evaluation problem: how collaborative workflows affect interactive qualitative coding. Its contribution is appropriately framed around evaluating existing systems rather than introducing another model.

The study involves 20 researchers, three substantially different systems, and a shared corpus of approximately 85,000 tweets. Holding initializations fixed within each system provides useful experimental control.

The evaluation combines consistency, cohesiveness, distinctiveness, 1,200 manually assessed document–theme pairs, and participant interviews. Double annotation with adjudication and reported agreement are valuable methodological elements.
weaknesses: The experimental conditions do not adequately establish the central collaboration claim. Section 4 compares three individual coders with two groups of three coders per tool. The individual outputs are never consolidated, although the introduction defines asynchronous collaboration as including consolidation. Participant allocation, reuse, experience balancing, and person-hours are unspecified. Consequently, collaboration modality is entangled with team size and potentially effort. An actual asynchronous collaboration condition or narrower individual-versus-group claims are needed.

The statistical evidence is insufficiently documented. Two synchronous codebooks provide only one codebook pair for consistency evaluation. Tables 1–2 report unpaired t-tests without identifying the observational unit, test sample sizes, or dependence handling. Themes within codebooks and comparisons sharing a codebook are dependent; treating them as independent replicates would exaggerate certainty. The paper needs analysis and uncertainty estimates that respect the experimental units, with additional replication or substantially more cautious claims.

The proposed metrics require stronger construct validation. Maximum-similarity matching permits many-to-one alignments and depends on theme number and granularity, yet theme counts and size distributions are absent. Centroid similarities of 0.94–0.98 provide little demonstrated discrimination. The manuscript does not establish that these scores track human judgments of equivalent or useful themes. These issues matter because the evaluation framework is itself a central contribution.

The correctness results are difficult to interpret and contain a substantive reporting inconsistency. Section 5 describes checking assigned document–theme pairs, which directly supports assignment precision, while Figure 4 reports F1 without defining recall, reference labels, or averaging. Confidence intervals and treatment of the LLM's 0.7–16.1% invalid-label outputs are unspecified. Moreover, Figure 4 favors synchronous topic coding at the second and third cumulative quartiles and shows equality overall, contrary to the text's claimed asynchronous advantage.

Conclusions about system families and interaction richness exceed the evidence. The LLM findings concern only Llama 3.2 3B-Instruct with one implementation and prompt-selection procedure. Appendix D even includes a candidate prompt referring to programming objects/classes and code functionality, without identifying which template each session selected. The relational system also receives stance and morality information, providing another explanation for performance differences. Conclusions about LLM scalability and interaction bandwidth should be restricted to the tested configurations unless these alternatives are examined.

Reproducibility remains incomplete despite useful appendix material. The manuscript omits the exact sentence-embedding checkpoint, LLM decoding settings, resulting codebooks, detailed correctness rubric, and statistical implementation; code and annotation outputs are only promised for future release. The interview evidence also lacks the number of completed interviews and an analysis procedure, while interview format differs by condition. These omissions limit verification of both the quantitative results and comparative user-experience claims.
